The key bill is **B2026-211** (Hill Country, Mesa Vista Unit 7B). Its diagnostic write-up says: *"12 yr Ruud RS75 water heater... Corrosion visible on burner assembly and tank base, thermocouple out, heat exchanger cracked. **Full unit replacement recommended, approx 1850 dollars for equal model swap. That directly contradicts the $310 "exchanger swap + thermocouple" summary. Let me gather the surrounding context before I act.

Let me set up tracking and check Thursday's calendar.

input.body:
**Scope landed: full water heater replacement — not the ~$310 exchanger+thermocouple patch.**

Two accounts were in play:
1. Hill Country's email summary (Diane, 6/29) and Tony's 6/29 #maintenance endorsement scoped only an exchanger swap + new thermocouple (~$310), leaning on "tank held pressure on the hold test" and staying on Robert's June budget.
2. The tech's actual diagnostic write-up on the bill (B2026-211, QBO vendor 201) documents a 12-yr Ruud RS75 with corrosion on the burner assembly **and tank base**, thermocouple out, and a **cracked heat exchanger** — and recommends **full unit replacement (~$1,850, equal-model)**, stating piecemeal repair is not advised on a unit this age.

The summary and the bill's diagnostic don't line up: the summary omitted the tank-base corrosion and cracked exchanger and inverted the recommendation. On an older unit the diagnostic detail governs, so we're going with full replacement. Last night's tenant escalation (no hot water since ~4 PM, spreading kitchen puddle, kids home) corroborates a failing unit; priority bumped to High.

Actions taken: Airtable MT-2026-1327 updated (High + full-replacement scope). Email drafts staged for Diane (revised confirmation to pull replacement parts), Tanya (rationale + Thursday-AM timing), and Robert (cost heads-up ~$1,850). Onsite block added Thu 7/2 AM (overlaps the 9:00–9:45 Las Vistas 9D kickoff — needs coverage/hand-off). Confirming with Hill Country pending final sign-off.

input.subject: Mesa Vista 7B — water heater replacement scheduled Thursday morning
input.body:

Rather than do a stopgap, we're replacing the whole unit so you have reliable hot water and no more leaking.

Timing for the week: Hill Country Plumbing is scheduled to replace it Thursday morning. They expect to be in and out that morning — the hot water will be off for a few hours during the swap and back on the same day. I'll be onsite when they arrive. If you can, please clear a little space around the water heater and keep the kids and any pets away from the work area that morning.

If the leak gets worse before then or you have any trouble, call me right away.

Thanks for your patience,
Carlos Mendez
Star Property Management

input.subject: Heads-up — Mesa Vista 7B water heater replacement (revised cost)
input.body:
Hi Robert,

A quick heads-up on a maintenance item at Mesa Vista Unit 7B. The tenant reported a small water-heater drip earlier this week and Hill Country Plumbing came out to diagnose it. Their first quick summary suggested a minor repair (heat exchanger and thermocouple, around $310). When I went through their full diagnostic on the unit — a 12-year-old Ruud — it found corrosion on the burner assembly and tank base and a cracked heat exchanger, and recommended full replacement rather than a piecemeal repair that wouldn't hold on a unit this age. The tenant then lost hot water entirely and had water spreading on the kitchen floor, which confirms the unit is failing.

Given that, I'm moving forward with a full water heater replacement — an equal-model swap at approximately $1,850, versus the ~$310 patch. It's more than the original estimate, but it avoids a repeat failure and further water damage, and it fits with the water-heater replacements we'd already flagged as a budget priority. This will land in July rather than June.

Hill Country is scheduled to install Thursday morning and I'll be onsite. Let me know if you have any questions.
